newsitem.title: USA: U.S. moves Asian migrants to Guantanamo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. moves Asian migrants to Guantanamo.

text.p: The United States has moved over 100 Asian migrants from a crowded freighter where they were living in brutal conditions to the U.S. naval base at Guantanamo Bay on Cuba, the State Department said on Wednesday.

But the Guantanamo Bay stop is only temporary, spokesman Nicholas Burns said. He indicated that as soon as next week the group would be moved to another location and questioned about their trip aboard the cargo vessel Xing Da.
Three New York men have been indicted in Massachusetts with attempting to smuggle the Asians into the United States by ship.
Burns said the refugees were "Asian and we suspect Chinese from a particular province in China."
"They will not be screened and they will not be interviewed by our law enforcement agencies and our immigration agencies at Guantanamo," Burns told reporters.
"They are being held there (at Guantanamo) simply so they can be fed and housed because they were living in unacceptable conditions on this refugee migrant ship."
"They will be taken to another location, probably as early as next week, so that they can be questioned by U.S. government authorities," Burns said. "This is a very mysterious case."
State Department spokeswoman Susan Snyder said eventually the group would be "transported to a place suitable for screening and for repatriation of those who it is appopriate to repatriate."
The Xing Da was found adrift last week in the Atlantic Ocean about 150 miles (240 km) off Bermuda. The vessel broke down at sea and the U.S. Coast Guard towed it into sheltered waters off Bermuda.
Burns said the ship had no electricity, a disabled engine and "very severe conditions for the people on board".

Officials in Bermuda said the 83 passengers and 23 crew were taken in ferries from the ship to Bermuda International Airport, where they were flown out of the British colony aboard U.S. Coast Guard C-130s.

They were transported to the planes in handcuffs under the watchful eyes of 100 members of the Bermuda Regiment, who were mobilized for the first time in a decade, since they were involved in the cleanup after Hurricane Emily in 1987.
Bob Farmer, the U.S. Consul in Bermuda, said the Xing Da was in "horrible shape," leaking fuel, taking on water and without functioning engines.
"The problems have been compounded by the uncooperative passengers, who lit fires, tossed feces at the Coast Guard personnel and nearly rioted on a few occasions," he said.
He said the Xing Da would be towed to Miami where it will be cleaned and sunk as an artificial reef.
The three men who were charged with attempting to smuggle the group into the United States are Hui Lin, 34, Yiu Ming Kwan, 45 and Nai Fook Li, 30, all of New York City.

Court documents in Massachusetts say the defendants had planned to offload the migrants into a smaller vessel to be brought to the Massachusetts shore. But the owner of the smaller ship was actually an undercover agent for the Immigration and Naturalisation Service.
The trio were charged with two counts of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and two counts of attempted alien smuggling.
